newsitem.title: UK: Rights group slams Belarus clampdown on expression.
newsitem.headline: Rights group slams Belarus clampdown on expression.

text.p: A New York-based human rights group on Thursday accused Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko of reversing most of the advances of the perestroika era and urged him to halt his government's attacks on free expression.
Human Rights Watch said the Belarus government had banned public discussion from the state-owned media and was now driving all independent media outlets out of business.

The group presented its report, "Belarus: Crushing Civil Society", in Minsk on the day the Belarus government arrested 14 journalists who were taking part in and reporting on the presentation of a petition in support of an arrested Russian television crew.
A summary of the report was made available in London.
The arrest of the three journalists from Russia's state-owned ORT network last Saturday has provoked a row with Moscow which is threatening to review agreements on closer links with Minsk.
Two of the journalists were charged on Wednesday with offences that could carry sentences of five years in prison.

Human Rights Watch said the Minsk government's campaign against Russian broadcast media was especially fierce because it dared to criticise its policies and offered the only television news alternative to state controlled television.
The group said the government had also targetted demonstrators and non-governmental organisations (NGOs).
"Human Rights Watch condemns the exorbitant fines on demonstrators and organizers levied recently after blatantly unfair trials.

"Excessive use of force by police to break up peaceful demonstrations is designed to spread terror among protestors and bystanders, rather than an attempt to maintain or restore public order," the group said.

It said NGOs were harrassed by "questionable tax audits and outrageous rent hikes," while independent print media were being marginalised by the government misusing its monopoly on publishing houses and issuing arbitrary tax regulations.
Human Rights Watch called on Minsk to restore freedom of speech and association, to end curbs on the media and to re-establish an independent judiciary.
It also urged Russia and the European Union to use their influence to persuade Minsk to do this.
